text: If you listen only to what women say, you'll be confused. If you watch what they do, things become clearer. In this series, I'll translate women's words and behavior into plain language and tell you what's the best way to react. Imagine you matched with a girl on a dating app or maybe you met her somewhere in real life. You exchange contacts and you decide to text her. She does reply. The interest isn't very high, but there is some conversation. You like her, so you decide to do the right move. You ask her out. You write something like, hey, what are your plans for the weekend? How about we grab a drink Friday or Saturday evening? But instead of a clear yes or no, she replies with something like, oh, I am busy this weekend. Now, this is where a lot of guys get stuck. How should you read that? Is she really busy? Should you wait or should you push more? Here's the key thing you need to understand. It depends on how she says she's busy. If it's a dry response, just I am busy with no explanation and no alternatives, you should generally perceive that as a no. You don't argue with it. You don't try to convince her. You don't send 10 follow ups. If you really want, you can still try one more time later, but wait a week or two and then ask her out again like nothing happened. But if she still does not give you a yes, that's where you normally stop and move on. Now, imagine she says she's busy, but she actually gives you the reason. She says that her parents are visiting or she will be out of town. Then she still might be interested. In that case, you stay relaxed and positive. You say something simple like, oh, nice, have a good time and let's check next week. And then next week you try again. The best sign is when she provides alternatives herself. For example, she says, sorry, I'm busy this weekend, but I am free on Tuesday. That's a green light. It usually means interest is there. At that point, you set the date and go see where it leads. Here's the general rule you should remember. When a woman is interested, she doesn't make things complicated. She helps you. When things stay vague, unclear, and one-sided, the interest usually isn't there. You don't take it personally. You don't overanalyze it. You move on and keep working on meeting someone else.
